finding_F105_STATUS_ITSELF_IS_PURCHASABL.claim: Qatar Airways sells the loyalty currency, the STATUS points, and a paid subscription to the loyalty programme itself.
finding_F105_STATUS_ITSELF_IS_PURCHASABL.confidence: Verified that these products exist as named destinations. Their mechanics and prices were NOT captured.

the_progression_across_four_programmes.Booking.com Genius: tenure only — 5 then 15 bookings. Nothing purchasable. Nothing earnable off-platform.
the_progression_across_four_programmes.Expedia One Key: currency + tier, both earned from bookings only.
the_progression_across_four_programmes.Iberia Club: currency earnable OFF-PLATFORM via 90+ retail brands (F-58); STATUS still flight-gated.
the_progression_across_four_programmes.Qatar Privilege Club: currency purchasable, STATUS purchasable, and a paid membership tier above the free programme.

finding_F105_STATUS_ITSELF_IS_PURCHASABL.why_it_matters_for_luma: F-58 identified the transferable idea as separating a SPENDABLE currency open to everyone from a STATUS ladder earned by use. Qatar collapses that separation entirely — status is a product. That is the logical endpoint of tenure-based loyalty and it is worth Luma seeing, because it shows the model's destination: if status can be bought, it no longer signals anything about the traveller, and the first-time traveller can simply pay to skip the ladder. Whether that is a feature or the death of the mechanism is a genuine strategic question.

finding_F106_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_PROD.claim: Qatar Airways treats the airport as a destination with its own product line, unlike Iberia where airport services are a Business-class entitlement.
evidence_from_navigation: Hamad International Airport — a dedicated site section
finding_F106_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_PROD.confidence: Verified that these destinations exist. Whether any is PURCHASABLE by an economy passenger was NOT determined — no pricing page was opened.

the_business_goal_5_position.the_goal_verbatim: Increase usage of airport services such as lounges and Fast Track (scenario.pdf)
the_business_goal_5_position.Iberia (F-53): 'Servicios VIP para la clase Business' — bundled with a fare class, no price anywhere
the_business_goal_5_position.Qatar: airport services exist as a named product line including an airport hotel and transit tours — a materially wider surface

finding_F106_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_PROD.why_this_does_NOT_close_F54: F-54 raised the real problem: if airport services come free with premium cabins, the addressable market for SELLING them is economy passengers, which is a business the scenario has not scoped and whose competitors — lounge aggregators — are absent from all four tiers. Qatar shows a wider surface but the pricing and eligibility question is untouched. F-54 stands.
finding_F106_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_PROD.note_on_transit_tours: A free or paid city tour during a layover is a genuinely distinctive answer to 'passengers often waste time waiting unnecessarily' — a problem the scenario names explicitly. Not pursued; recorded as the single most Luma-relevant item on this competitor's homepage.

finding_F107_DISRUPTION_ABSENT_FROM_NAVI.claim: No disruption, delay, cancellation, compensation or passenger-rights destination appears in Qatar Airways' 289 homepage links.
finding_F107_DISRUPTION_ABSENT_FROM_NAVI.method: All 289 link labels swept for disrupt/delay/cancel/irregular/compensat/rights/refund. Zero matches.

the_pattern_across_tier_4.Iberia: names the operational-disruption regime on its changes page, provides no link; 367+ labels searched, zero (F-56)
the_pattern_across_tier_4.American Airlines: publishes a Customer Service Plan with four named disruption sections (F-104) — though reached by URL, not by navigation

finding_F107_DISRUPTION_ABSENT_FROM_NAVI.the_careful_conclusion: Two of three airlines do not surface disruption in their primary navigation. The third publishes a structured plan whose FINDABILITY is untested. This strengthens F-104's conclusion that disruption handling is a product choice — but the symmetric findability test is owed on both American Airlines and Qatar before the comparison is sound.
finding_F107_DISRUPTION_ABSENT_FROM_NAVI.for_luma: Across three airlines, the moment a traveller most needs help is the moment hardest to navigate to. That is the consistent observation of the entire round — F-56, F-57, F-90, F-104 and now F-107 all point at the same gap from different angles.

method_note_two_404s.observed: Two URL guesses returned 404s this session — American Airlines ('This page must have taken flight') and Qatar Airways ('Page not found | Qatar Airways').
method_note_two_404s.the_failure: My own is404 check read the first 300 characters of BODY text. Qatar's 404 announced itself only in the <title>. The check returned FALSE on a 404.
method_note_two_404s.corrected_rule: Check document.title AND body for 404 markers before extracting anything. Seventh instance this round of a result that looks like data and is not.
method_note_two_404s.why_it_matters: A 404 that passes an extraction sweep produces findings about a page that does not exist. Recorded so the next operator does not repeat it.
